words.defn_en: to understand, know, become aware of:

sentences.en: It took her a while to ______ the subtle change in her friend's mood.
sentences.zh: 她過了一會兒才察覺到朋友情緒上細微的變化。

sentences.en: Many people ______ the new policy as unfair to small businesses.
sentences.zh: 許多人認為這項新政策對小型企業不公平。

words.defn_en: just beginning to exist:

sentences.en: Doctors were able to treat the ______ stage of the disease before it spread.
sentences.zh: 醫生得以在疾病擴散之前治療這個初期階段。

sentences.en: The manager noticed ______ signs of conflict between the two employees.
sentences.zh: 經理注意到這兩名員工之間初現的衝突跡象。

words.defn_en: disabled, made unfit:

sentences.en: The accident left him temporarily ______ and unable to work.
sentences.zh: 這場意外讓他暫時失去行動能力,無法工作。

sentences.en: The injured player was completely ______ for the rest of the season.
sentences.zh: 這名受傷的球員在本季剩餘的時間裡完全無法上場。

words.defn_en: easily affected:

sentences.en: Young children are especially ______ to colds in winter.
sentences.zh: 幼童在冬天特別容易感冒。

sentences.en: People under stress are more ______ to making impulsive decisions.
sentences.zh: 處於壓力之下的人更容易做出衝動的決定。

words.defn_en: made for the sake of quarreling; quibbling

sentences.en: The editor's ______ remarks focused on trivial grammar mistakes.
sentences.zh: 這位編輯吹毛求疵的評論只盯著一些瑣碎的文法錯誤。

sentences.en: His ______ criticism made it hard for anyone to please him.
sentences.zh: 他吹毛求疵的批評讓任何人都很難讓他滿意。

words.defn_en: the start, the beginning of something

sentences.en: The company has grown tremendously since its ______ ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 自從十年前創立以來,這家公司已有了長足的發展。

sentences.en: He has led the project from its ______ to its final launch.
sentences.zh: 他從這項計畫一開始就領導著它,直到最終上線。

words.defn_en: to expect or predict:

sentences.en: Does the weatherman ______ a rise in temperatures next week?
sentences.zh: 氣象預報員是否預期下週氣溫會上升?

sentences.en: We ______ a busy weekend at the store due to the sale.
sentences.zh: 由於這次特賣,我們預期商店這個週末會很忙碌。

words.defn_en: a thick rope or bundle of wires; a message sent by underwater telegraph:

sentences.en: Engineers checked every ______ supporting the suspension bridge.
sentences.zh: 工程師檢查了支撐這座吊橋的每一條纜繩。

sentences.en: The soldier sent a brief ______ home to reassure his worried family.
sentences.zh: 這名士兵發了一封簡短的電報回家,安撫擔心的家人。

words.defn_en: very spacious:

sentences.en: Her ______ handbag could fit a laptop, an umbrella, and a change of clothes.
sentences.zh: 她那容量寬大的手提包可以裝下筆電、雨傘和一套換洗衣物。

sentences.en: The mansion's ______ living room could easily host a hundred guests.
sentences.zh: 這棟豪宅寬敞的客廳可以輕鬆容納上百位賓客。

words.defn_en: the act of surrendering or giving in, especially under agreed conditions:

sentences.en: The general's ______ ended the three-year siege without further bloodshed.
sentences.zh: 這位將軍的投降,結束了長達三年的圍城,未再流血。

sentences.en: Critics saw the new policy as a ______ to industry lobbyists.
sentences.zh: 評論家將這項新政策視為向產業說客屈服的表現。

words.defn_en: a sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behavior:

sentences.en: The queen's ______ meant courtiers never knew which policy would be favored next.
sentences.zh: 這位女王反覆無常的性情,讓朝臣永遠猜不透下一個受青睞的政策是什麼。

sentences.en: He bought the sports car on a ______ , then regretted it within a month.
sentences.zh: 他一時心血來潮買了這輛跑車,結果不到一個月就後悔了。

words.defn_en: the tendency to find fault or raise petty objections:

sentences.en: Her ______ during meetings made even simple proposals feel like interrogations.
sentences.zh: 她在會議上愛挑剔的態度,讓連最簡單的提案都彷彿變成一場審訊。

sentences.en: The critic's reputation for ______ meant few directors sought his approval.
sentences.zh: 這位評論家以愛挑剔聞名,因此很少有導演會渴望得到他的肯定。

words.defn_en: to get the attention of, hold:

sentences.en: The magician's tricks ______d the audience of children.
sentences.zh: 這位魔術師的把戲讓這群孩子觀眾看得如癡如醉。

sentences.en: Her vivid storytelling never fails to ______ a room.
sentences.zh: 她生動的說故事方式總是能讓全場為之著迷。

words.defn_en: fascinated or attracted intensely:

sentences.en: The children sat ______ as the storyteller began her tale.
sentences.zh: 說書人一開始講故事,孩子們就聽得入迷。

sentences.en: Audiences were completely ______ by the acrobat's daring performance.
sentences.zh: 觀眾完全被這位特技演員大膽的表演給迷住了。

words.defn_en: capturing interest or attention; charming:

sentences.en: Her ______ smile was the first thing everyone noticed.
sentences.zh: 她迷人的笑容是大家第一眼就注意到的。

sentences.en: The documentary offers a ______ look into the lives of deep-sea creatures.
sentences.zh: 這部紀錄片對深海生物的生活提供了引人入勝的一瞥。

words.defn_en: a main division of a book; a distinct period in someone's life:

sentences.en: The final ______ ties together every loose thread in the novel.
sentences.zh: 最後一章將小說中所有的伏筆全部收尾。

sentences.en: Moving abroad marked a whole new ______ in her life.
sentences.zh: 移居國外標誌著她人生嶄新的一個階段。

words.defn_en: feelings of excessive pride:

sentences.en: His ______ made it impossible for him to admit he was wrong.
sentences.zh: 他的自負讓他不可能承認自己犯了錯。

sentences.en: Despite his fame, he showed surprisingly little ______.
sentences.zh: 儘管聲名遠播,他表現得卻出奇地不自負。

words.defn_en: to form a concept or idea of something in one's mind:

sentences.en: She ______ a new business model that revolutionized the industry.
sentences.zh: 她構思出一套徹底改變業界的新商業模式。

sentences.en: In this lab, scientists ______ new theories on viruses.
sentences.zh: 在這間實驗室裡,科學家們構思關於病毒的新理論。

words.defn_en: misleading or giving a false impression:

sentences.en: The advertisement was ______, leading customers to believe the product was free.
sentences.zh: 這則廣告具有誤導性,讓顧客誤以為這項產品是免費的。

sentences.en: The advertisement was ______ in its claims of weight loss.
sentences.zh: 這則廣告在減重功效的宣稱上具有欺騙性。

words.defn_en: to free someone from legal, social, or political restriction:
words.root_note: e- (out) + manus (hand) + capere (to take), from Latin

sentences.en: The proclamation aimed to ______ enslaved people.
sentences.zh: 這項宣言旨在解放被奴役的人民。

sentences.en: Education can ______ individuals from poverty.
sentences.zh: 教育能使個人擺脫貧窮的束縛。

words.defn_en: unusually excellent; not typical:

sentences.en: Her ______ talent was obvious from a young age.
sentences.zh: 她從小就展現出明顯的傑出才華。

sentences.en: These are ______ circumstances that call for a different plan.
sentences.zh: 這是異常的情況,需要不同的應對計畫。

words.defn_en: relating to a town or city with local self-government:
words.root_note: municipium (self-governing town), from Latin munia (duties) + capere (to take)

sentences.en: The city council approved funding for the new ______ park.
sentences.zh: 市議會核准了這座新市立公園的經費。

sentences.en: ______ elections determine who leads the local government.
sentences.zh: 市政選舉決定了誰將領導地方政府。

words.defn_en: to take up space or time:

sentences.en: The kids ______ themselves with games.
sentences.zh: 孩子們用遊戲來打發時間。

sentences.en: The army continued to ______ the border town for several years.
sentences.zh: 軍隊持續佔領這座邊境城鎮長達數年之久。

words.defn_en: able to be noticed or perceived:
words.root_note: percipere (to perceive), from Latin per- (thoroughly) + capere (to seize)

sentences.en: There was a barely ______ change in her tone of voice.
sentences.zh: 她的語氣有著幾乎難以察覺的變化。

sentences.en: The tremor was hardly ______ to those far from the epicenter.
sentences.zh: 對於遠離震央的人來說,這場地震幾乎難以察覺。

words.defn_en: having or showing keen insight or understanding:
words.root_note: percipere (to perceive), from Latin per- (thoroughly) + capere (to seize)

sentences.en: Her ______ comments revealed a deep understanding of the text.
sentences.zh: 她敏銳的評論展現了她對這篇文章深刻的理解。

sentences.en: The ______ therapist quickly identified the source of his anxiety.
sentences.zh: 這位敏銳的治療師迅速找出了他焦慮的根源。

words.defn_en: having or showing keen perception or insight:
words.defn_zh: 有感知力的;有洞察力的人
words.root_note: percipere (to perceive), from Latin per- (thoroughly) + capere (to seize)

sentences.en: A ______ observer would have noticed the subtle discrepancy immediately.
sentences.zh: 一位敏銳的觀察者會立刻注意到這個細微的差異。

sentences.en: The witness proved unusually ______ under cross-examination.
sentences.zh: 這位證人在交叉詰問下展現出異常敏銳的觀察力。

words.defn_en: a brief summary of what has previously been stated:
words.root_note: shortened form of recapitulation, from Latin re- (again) + capitulum (chapter)

sentences.en: The teacher gave a quick ______ of last week's lesson.
sentences.zh: 這位老師簡短概括了上週的課程內容。

sentences.en: Let's ______ the main points before moving on to the next topic.
sentences.zh: 在進入下一個主題之前,讓我們先概括一下重點。

words.defn_en: a summary of the main points at the end of a discussion or text:
words.root_note: recapitulare (to sum up), from Latin re- (again) + capitulum (chapter)

sentences.en: The final chapter offers a ______ of all the book's central arguments.
sentences.zh: 最後一章對整本書的核心論點提供了一份總結概述。

sentences.en: The presentation ended with a clear ______ of the proposed solutions.
sentences.zh: 這場簡報以清楚概述所提出的解決方案作為結尾。

words.defn_en: open to new ideas:

sentences.en: The new dancer was ______ to feedback.
sentences.zh: 這位新來的舞者很樂於接受回饋意見。

sentences.en: Investors seemed ______ to the startup's innovative pitch.
sentences.zh: 投資人似乎對這家新創公司創新的提案抱持開放的態度。
